paths.description: apps.facebook.com redirect, public login and first-load cookie consent; primary accessible archetype
Public account-creation archetype; first-load consent state inspected, account creation not submitted
Public account-recovery archetype; first-load consent state inspected, recovery not submitted
Authenticated Facebook app/feed and account-management journeys; excluded because no authorized test account was supplied

findings.summary: The public login and consent UI ignore the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode capture is visually identical to the light capture; DOM computed styles report color-scheme: normal and a white body/dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint surfaces, text, borders, and controls under prefers-color-scheme using semantic color tokens.

findings.summary: A full-screen cookie consent dialog obscures the entire primary login experience on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the page dimmed behind a modal that occupies most of the usable viewport before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the first-layer consent explanation, keep both choices immediately available, and reserve detail for an expandable secondary view.

findings.summary: The consent modal is implemented as a custom div rather than the native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe finds DIV role=dialog aria-modal=true and no dialog element.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog with showModal(), an accessible name, and platform dismissal behavior while retaining the clear consent actions.

findings.summary: The desktop login document does not set a viewport meta tag, causing a 980 CSS-pixel layout to be scaled down on a 360px screen.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout reports hasViewportMeta:false, innerWidth 980, and visual scale 0.367; the screenshot renders the dialog and footer at tiny text sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and rebuild the public login/consent layout with intrinsic fluid sizing at narrow viewports.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the first focusable login input.
findings.evidence: The focus probe programmatically focuses the email input and reads outline:none and box-shadow:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and verify focus on all links, fields, consent controls, and custom role=button elements.

findings.summary: The public login experience paints far too late.
findings.evidence: The DevTools trace measured FCP/LCP at 7.22s; Lighthouse measured FCP 6.3s and LCP 7.7s with performance 0.58.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the login/consent critical path, reduce server/document latency, and defer nonessential scripts, styles, and font work.

findings.summary: Late layout movement and unreserved consent imagery reduce visual stability.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.085; all four consent images lack complete width/height dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width and height (or aspect-ratio) on consent media and reserve all late content space.

findings.summary: Main-thread work includes blocking tasks during the delayed paint.
findings.evidence: The trace reports two long tasks, longest 141ms, and 156.7ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Split startup work, schedule nonessential tasks after the critical login UI, and remove avoidable synchronous initialization.

findings.summary: A simple public login/consent surface transfers a heavy startup payload.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 43 requests and 2.05MB transferred, including 1.33MB script, 324KB CSS, and a 183KB font; a parser-inserted VeryHigh stylesheet is on the critical path.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a minimal unauthenticated bundle, inline only critical CSS, preload only the actual critical font/resource, and defer the rest.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated page ships 24 scripts and multiple large bundles before the user can log in.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 24 script requests and 1.33MB transferred; the largest script is 298KB and Lighthouse flags missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit coverage and split the login/consent route so authenticated-product modules are not loaded before authentication.

findings.summary: The mobile login variant contains incomplete ARIA and unlabeled form controls.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility score is 0.78 and fails aria-required-attr and label audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native controls where possible and ensure every role has required ARIA and every form control has a programmatic label.

findings.summary: Some foreground/background combinations fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the color-contrast audit on the mobile login variant.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust affected text and control colors to meet WCAG AA in default, dimmed, and consent states.

findings.summary: The public page lacks semantic landmarks/headings and suppresses visible focus.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe finds zero h1 and no main/nav/header/footer landmarks; focused email input has no outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1, a main landmark and appropriate navigation/footer landmarks, then implement a coherent visible focus order.

findings.summary: The mobile variant constrains scaling and the desktop response omits a device-width viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout evidence shows no viewport meta on the rendered desktop response; Lighthouse fails meta-viewport because the mobile response limits scaling below the audit threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an accessible viewport policy that permits zoom and ensure all public routes reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: The login load logs browser console errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the errors-in-console audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the recorded network/runtime errors and add production monitoring that treats unauthenticated-route console errors as regressions.

findings.summary: Consent images omit complete intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports all four images missing a height attribute; the layout observer records CLS 0.085.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit complete intrinsic dimensions for every image and retain the correct aspect ratio.

findings.summary: The page uses deprecated behavior and is not eligible for the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecated API warning and four BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use and address unload/cache-control/runtime blockers so login, recovery, and signup history navigation can use BFCache.

findings.summary: The public landing page has only a generic title and no meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM probe reports title “Facebook” and description:null.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a route-specific title and concise description for the public login/landing experience.

findings.summary: Non-JavaScript crawlers receive almost none of the visible public content.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 1% raw/rendered word coverage, classified the response as a JS shell, and captured a blank crawler screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the public page purpose, heading, login/recovery links, and essential consent information as semantic HTML with real hrefs.

findings.summary: The CSP still permits unsafe inline styles.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and CSP, but the style-src policy includes unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate inline styles to nonce/hash-authorized styles and tighten style-src without weakening the existing CSP.

findings.summary: The main response omits an explicit Referrer-Policy header.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports referrer-policy missing while HSTS, X-Frame-Options and Permissions-Policy are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a deliberate Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin and verify redirect and outbound-link behavior.

findings.summary: The public page is effectively blank without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability captured an empty crawler view and 1% content coverage despite 1,954 rendered text characters.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render essential login, recovery, signup and consent content, then progressively enhance interactions.

findings.summary: The password field omits an autocomplete token.
findings.evidence: DOM probe reports username webauthn on the identity field but an empty autocomplete value on the password field.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete=current-password and preserve username webauthn; verify password-manager and passkey conditional UI behavior.

findings.summary: Consent imagery uses legacy PNG files without responsive sources or lazy loading below the fold.
findings.evidence: Images evidence reports four PNGs, all missing srcset and loading=lazy; each is below the fold.
findings.suggestedFix: Use appropriately compressed modern formats, responsive sources, and lazy loading for below-fold explanatory media.

findings.summary: The login/consent route performs disproportionate startup work for its narrow purpose.
findings.evidence: HAR records 43 requests and 2.05MB, including 24 scripts, before authentication; trace still records long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a strict unauthenticated-route budget and delay product, analytics, and nonessential modules until needed or after consent/authentication.

findings.summary: Cross-origin delivery dominates the app-origin request profile.
findings.evidence: Relative to apps.facebook.com, HAR attributes 34 requests and 2.052MB to other origins, primarily static.xx.fbcdn.net; even accounting for same-owner CDN delivery, the payload is disproportionate to a login form.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce script/font payload and request count, cache aggressively, and load optional media only when its detail panel is opened.

findings.summary: The initial heap footprint is high for a public login and consent surface.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contains about 860k nodes/heap entries and 43.8MB self size; post-focus-cycle snapshot remains about 44.0MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the unauthenticated bundle and remove product modules, large registries, and retained initialization state not needed for login.

findings.summary: The consent design gives the acceptance choice stronger visual emphasis than rejection.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show “Allow all cookies” as the filled blue primary action while “Decline optional cookies” is visually secondary, despite both being valid choices.
findings.suggestedFix: Give accept and decline comparable prominence and keep the purpose and consequences equally clear.
